item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal math
item.description: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
item.content: Inspect ledgerly/money.py and models.py first to learn the money policy. Wrap inputs with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round results with round_money so rounding and type conventions match the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Guard division with a zero-total check
item.description: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator before dividing and return the documented fallback (ZERO) when it is zero.
item.content: Compute total_quantity first; if it is falsy, return ZERO immediately. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement and avoids ZeroDivisionError without try/except.

item.title: Read the target module and tests before editing
item.description: Start by reading the file to be modified, related models/utilities, and any existing tests for the feature to align signatures and behavior.
item.content: Cat invoice.py, models.py, money.py, and tests/test_average_unit_price.py before writing code. This reveals the exact stub signature, dataclass field names (line.quantity, line.unit_price), and expected return type, enabling a first-attempt pass.

item.title: Match existing error codes and validation patterns before implementing
item.description: Grep the codebase for similar validation (state checks, amount checks) to reuse established BillingError codes and message formats.
item.content: Before writing validation logic, search for existing patterns like `invalid_state` or `negative_amount` in sibling modules. Reusing the same error codes and f-string message formats keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on codes.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer types
item.description: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(x, int) accepts True/False; explicitly reject bools for integer-only parameters.
item.content: When a parameter must be a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before the range check. Otherwise True would pass as quantity 1 and silently corrupt data.

item.title: Normalize money inputs through the project's to_money helper
item.description: Convert raw unit_price values with the existing to_money/round_money utilities before comparing or storing, rather than assuming Decimal.
item.content: Call `to_money(unit_price)` to coerce inputs, then compare against the module's ZERO constant for negativity. This handles ints, strings, and Decimals uniformly and keeps stored LineItem values consistent with the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Reuse existing timezone-normalization helpers
item.description: When implementing date arithmetic, normalize inputs with the repo's existing UTC helper rather than assuming tz-awareness.
item.content: Before writing datetime logic, grep for helpers like ensure_utc in sibling modules (e.g. subscriptions.current_period) and apply them to all inputs. This keeps behavior consistent with the rest of the codebase and avoids naive/aware comparison errors.

item.title: Compute periodic occurrences with floor division
item.description: For 'first occurrence strictly after t' with fixed period from a start, use (t - start) // period then add one period.
item.content: Compute n = (after - start) // length, then renewal = start + (n+1)*length, with a small while-loop guard to enforce strict inequality. Handle after < start separately by returning start + length, since the start itself is not a renewal.

item.title: Verify edge cases with a quick script after tests pass
item.description: Passing tests isn't enough; probe boundary inputs (exact boundary, before start, just-before boundary) with an ad-hoc script.
item.content: After the test suite passes, run a short inline Python snippet exercising exact-boundary, pre-start, and off-by-one-second cases. This catches strict-vs-inclusive semantics bugs that a single happy-path test misses.

item.title: Idempotency must survive audit.clear()
item.description: The team convention requires calling audit.clear() after writing, which destroys the audit-based idempotency lookup; a separate persistent registry is needed.
item.content: When a convention says 'check audit.events() for the key' but another says 'call audit.clear() after each write', the audit log cannot be the idempotency store. Keep a module-level dict mapping idempotency_key -> result (or payment id) and consult it first, before state validation, so repeated calls return the original record without re-applying.

item.title: Read all conventions before designing the signature
item.description: The first attempt missed the approval-threshold and idempotency conventions entirely, causing rejection; the final diff added them but still failed.
item.content: Scan the full convention list up front and bake every cross-cutting requirement (keyword-only idempotency_key, keyword-only approved_by, audit.clear()) into the function signature and control flow from the start, rather than implementing the core logic first and patching conventions later.

item.title: Verify money/state helpers against real models
item.description: Refund logic depends on Payment fields (amount, refunded_amount, status) and money helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO); confirm their exact semantics before writing comparisons.
item.content: Inspect models.py and money.py to confirm field names, Decimal vs float types, and rounding behavior, then compare rounded Decimals consistently (e.g. refunded + amount > payment.amount) and set status to 'refunded' only when the running total equals the captured amount.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of raw arithmetic
item.description: When implementing a pricing/money function, inspect the repo's money module and reuse its conversion and rounding helpers.
item.content: Before writing arithmetic, read sibling modules (e.g. money.py, payments.py) to find helpers like to_money/round_money and constants like ZERO. Using them keeps rounding and type handling consistent with the rest of the codebase and matches hidden-test expectations.

item.title: Match the project's error type and code conventions
item.description: Grep for existing raise statements to learn which exception class and code-string style the project uses before adding validation.
item.content: Validation errors should use the project's domain exception (e.g. BillingError(code, message)) with a short snake_case code, not bare ValueError, unless the surrounding module already uses ValueError. Grep for 'invalid_', 'non_positive', etc. to mirror naming.

item.title: Read the visible tests to pin down input/output types
item.description: Check tests and call sites to determine whether inputs are Decimal, float, or int, and what return type is expected.
item.content: A test like add_tax(Decimal('100.00'), 8) == 108 reveals Decimal inputs and numeric comparison. Normalize inputs through the project's money helper and return the rounded money type so equality checks pass.

item.title: Check idempotency against the audit log, not a private registry
item.description: The team convention requires looking up prior operations via ledgerly.audit.events() by idempotency_key; inventing a module-level dict diverges from the convention and breaks across processes.
item.content: When a convention says 'if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result', implement exactly that lookup. Do not substitute a private in-memory registry, and do not reason that audit.clear() makes the log unusable — follow the stated mechanism.

item.title: Reconcile conflicting conventions before coding
item.description: The idempotency convention depends on audit.events() while the clear() convention empties the log; the agent resolved this by abandoning the audit log instead of flagging the conflict.
item.content: When two stated conventions appear to conflict, prefer the explicit lookup mechanism named in the convention and surface the tension rather than silently redesigning the approach. Deviating from a named API is a common rejection cause.

item.title: Apply the full convention checklist to every new mutating function
item.description: The first attempt omitted idempotency_key entirely; the final attempt added it but still used the wrong lookup source and ordering.
item.content: For any function that changes a payment/credit/invoice balance: add keyword-only idempotency_key=None, check the key before state validation, return the original record on a hit, include idempotency_key in the audit entry, and call audit.clear() after recording.
